newsitem.title: INDIA: India UTI retains 20 pct div on 96/97 US-64 scheme.
newsitem.headline: India UTI retains 20 pct div on 96/97 US-64 scheme.

text.p: The Unit Trust of India (UTI), the country's largest mutual fund, on Monday said it had set a 20 percent dividend for 1996/97 on its US-64 scheme, unchanged from the previous year.
In a statement, UTI said sales under various schemes, in the year under review, exceeded 91 billion rupees.
It said its investible funds were up at around 580 billion rupees against 566.2 billion rupees previously.
UTI said repurchases under ongoing schemes fell by 63 percent.
UTI chairman C.G. Gupta said he expected 1997/98 (April-March) to be good for the mutual fund industry.
"The macro-economic signs in the last few months have been positive," Gupta told a news conference while releasing the results of India's largest mutual fund, whose own financial year ends June 30.
"The economy seems to be recovering...if this is maintained, the prospects for the capital market are good and in turn mutual funds should do well."
Gupta said UTI planned to raise 120-150 billion rupees through various schemes in 1997/98.
